column1: # UTF-8 and CESU-8 whole-buffer codec corpus (Issue #443, parent #267).
# One row freezes one conversion of the production converters CUtf8::Utf8ToUni and CUtf8::UniToUtf8
# (sakura_core/charset/CUtf8.cpp). C++ production, the Rust candidate (sakura_document_codec) and an
# independent Rust scalar model must all agree with every row; the C++ suite Utf8CodecContract proves the
# rows against production, so a row never records anything production does not do.
# Columns (tab separated; blank lines and lines starting with '#' are ignored):
#   id         unique, lower-case letters, digits and '-'
#   class      the behavior the row exercises (the contract suite requires every class to be present)
#   direction  decode: bytes -> UTF-16 units; encode: UTF-16 units -> bytes
#   variants   both: UTF-8 and CESU-8 give the same expectation; utf8 or cesu8: that mode only
#   input      decode: bytes as 2-digit hex tokens; encode: UTF-16 units as 4-digit hex tokens;
#              tokens are separated by one space and '-' is the empty sequence
#   output     decode: UTF-16 units (4 digits); encode: bytes (2 digits)
#   lossy      1 when the production result is RESULT_LOSESOME (an unpaired surrogate outside
#              U+DC00..U+DCFF became '?'), else 0; always 0 for decode
# Rules the rows pin: every byte that does not start a complete valid sequence becomes the unit
# 0xDC00 + byte and the scan resumes at the next byte; a unit in U+DC00..U+DCFF that is not the low half of a pair
# encodes back to its low 8 bits as one byte; any other unpaired surrogate encodes to '?' and sets lossy.
# CESU-8 reads a surrogate pair only as two consecutive three-byte forms (high then low) and never
